source_quotes.BRIEF.md:3: Create coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone. (apostrophe normalized)
source_quotes.BRIEF.md:5: Assets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.
source_quotes.BRIEF.md:7: Update: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.
source_quotes.BRIEF.md:9: Current update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:3 fixes 16 by 16 logical cells and makes Ready static; BRIEF.md:9 keeps the 16x16 canvas and static behavior; src/queue-view.ts:6 declares frames 1 and :9 declares cell [16,16]. Left open: everything else.
comparisons.literal_check: Decoded image is exactly 16x16 pixels with a single static frame (no horizontal strip, no extra canvas).
comparisons.additions: None. 'No horizontal strip, no extra canvas' restates exactly-16x16-single-frame.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: None exists; a brief-conforming Ready is necessarily a 16x16 static image.
comparisons.bounds: BRIEF.md [3,3] and [9,9]; src/queue-view.ts [6,6] and [9,9] all pin the quoted lines (verified).
comparisons.disposition: Accept unchanged text; bounds corrected from [3,9]/[3,11].

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:3 'Use transparent backgrounds'; BRIEF.md:9 'Keep the existing ... transparent background'. The brief says nothing about alpha depth, edge treatment, glows or backing shapes.
comparisons.literal_check: The cell exterior is transparent: pixels that are not part of the subject (the check mark plus any deliberate edge treatment, glow or backing shape) have alpha 0, and no opaque or translucent matte, box or canvas fill covers the cell as an unintended background. Partial alpha on subject pixels, including authored soft edges, is permitted; binary alpha is not required.
comparisons.additions: The check defines 'subject' to include deliberate edge treatment, glow or backing shape, and rejects only an unintended matte/box/canvas fill. This widens, not narrows, relative to the historical 'no ... fringe fills the cell' wording.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A check with authored partial-alpha edge pixels or a deliberate soft glow and a fully transparent exterior: conforms to the brief and passes the new text (the old text could have rejected it as 'fringe'). A full-cell 10 percent tint: the brief's 'transparent background' excludes it and the new text rejects it as a translucent canvas fill. No conforming alternative is rejected.
comparisons.disposition: Accept clarified wording; it follows the PIXL profile's transparency/subject-construction distinction and keeps the owner outcome.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:9 'Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion.' src/queue.ts:3 ok -> succeeded; src/queue-view.ts:6 succeeded -> label Ready, this file; src/queue-view.ts:3 and assets/start.svg:1 identify the only existing sibling asset, the Start triangle. Left open: arm ratio, stroke width, caps, backing shape, palette, highlights.
comparisons.literal_check: Viewed alone at the declared display conditions, Ready visibly uses a check mark with asymmetrical arms (one arm clearly shorter than the other) and reads as successful completion. It must not read as the existing idle Start triangle (assets/start.svg), and it must not read generically as activity, failure or pause. Comparison against actual Working, Retry and Paused art is a deferred family obligation, not part of this check.
comparisons.additions: (a) '(one arm clearly shorter than the other)' explicates 'asymmetrical arms' as unequal length. (b) 'must not read as the existing idle Start triangle' is supported by the sibling asset in the same statusVisuals map. (c) 'must not read generically as activity, failure or pause' is entailed by conveying completion. (d) The family comparison is explicitly excluded from this check and deferred.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: For (a): a V with equal-length arms and unequal stroke weight. I judge the source itself excludes it: 'check mark' conventionally names a short stroke meeting a longer stroke, so the parenthetical adds no rejection the owner's term does not already make; no arm ratio is imposed. On my finding the revision-2 basis now states explicitly that this is the specialist's reading. For (b)-(c): a thin check, a check on a plate, a check with a 1:2 ratio all pass; no conforming alternative is rejected. The historical pointer to BRIEF.md:3 'working loop ... without looking like success' was correctly dropped: that sentence binds Working and is retained as the deferred obligation family-working-not-success.
comparisons.disposition: Accept; the explication is labelled as specialist reading in revision 2.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:3 'readable silhouettes' and 'Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel'; BRIEF.md:9 keeps the review display conditions; src/queue-view.ts:9 supplies the actual panel #172336, scale 3, nearest.
comparisons.literal_check: Composited on #172336, the silhouette is readable at 1x and at 3x nearest-neighbor scale, with no essential detail lost into the panel colour.
comparisons.additions: 'No essential detail lost into the panel colour' operationalizes readable; no numeric threshold. #172336/scale 3/nearest are consumer observations resolving 'the actual dark panel', now labelled as such in the basis.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A differently constructed but readable silhouette passes; a contrast ratio or component count is not required. None rejected.
comparisons.disposition: Accept unchanged text with corrected bounds and basis attribution.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:3 'Use ... the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required.' The brief names a colour role (accent) and leaves palette and extent open. assets/start.svg:1 fill #70b9ed is an observation of the existing accent, not an approved palette.
comparisons.literal_check: The existing UI's cool blue accent is visibly used in the mark so that its relationship to the Start control's fill (assets/start.svg, observed #70b9ed) is perceptible when both appear in the same status row. This is a visual relationship judgement: it does not require an exact hex value, a palette count, or that cool blue be the dominant or only colour.
comparisons.additions: The historical clause 'The dominant colour treatment' is removed. 'When both appear in the same status row' is a viewing context derived from statusCell/compactStatus sharing one statusVisuals map (src/queue-view.ts:3, :6, :10-11), not a restriction.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A mostly neutral light-grey check with a clear cool-blue edge or inner stroke: uses the accent perceptibly, conforms to the brief, would have been rejected by the historical 'dominant' clause, and passes the corrected check. The brief does not exclude it, so removing 'dominant' from the rejection rule is correct. The delivered sample's sole flat #70b9ed fill is recorded in the packet choices as a specialist extent choice; that attribution agrees with the PIXL profile's 'Visual roles' guidance.
comparisons.disposition: Accept the demotion; owner outcome preserved; extent choice recorded with scope.

comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:3 'Create coherent pixel-art status assets'; BRIEF.md:5 'propose a representative status sample before expanding the family'. These give a coherence goal and a sample-first process, not a construction recipe.
comparisons.literal_check: As a representative family sample, the image shows deliberate pixel-art construction: readable pixel clusters with consistent edge stepping, no accidental stray pixels, no resampling blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts (authored anti-aliasing or sub-pixel shading is not an artifact), and a stroke and colour treatment that could plausibly be carried to Working, Retry and Paused.
comparisons.additions: 'Consistent edge stepping' and 'plausibly carried to the family' are expert quality judgements. 'Blur' is narrowed to resampling blur so authored anti-aliasing (permitted by the open palette/alpha policy) is not rejected.
comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A check with deliberately anti-aliased diagonals in two or three blue tones: brief-conforming; the historical text could reject it as 'blur'; the corrected text does not. An intentionally irregular-stepped organic shape could fail 'consistent edge stepping'; that is an expert preference, which is why the criterion is a proposal scoped to this sample and explicitly does not approve the family style or bind Working, Retry or Paused.
comparisons.bounds: BRIEF.md [3,3] and [5,5] (verified; the historical single [3,9] pointer that cited two lines is split).
comparisons.disposition: Accept as a scoped expert proposal with explicit basis and scope; it binds nothing beyond this sample.
